name: html-escape-span
what: time of one call of the html escape for one value, in a loop over a list of values that moves the output position by the count, as a render does; ns per value
purpose_in_the_task_list: Task c08c8baf (the escape and its room), plan A4, after commit 6: below 32 bytes the html escape of include/ (arm 3) runs its scalar loop through table_escaped_into, which stores at room.data() + count; the form of 738ff29 stored through a pointer. Arm 4 stores through a std::span that each word advances. The run asks whether that form removes the cells where arm 3 was above arm 0 in html-escape-span-20261114T083204Z.json
method: not the method of mbedded-cbor/bench/README.md: one run, 6 rounds, the arm order alternates by round (forward, then reversed), each process 5 repetitions of 2^22 input bytes for each input, timed with std::chrono::steady_clock; arm 1 is arm 0 built twice; sysbench cpu 10 times for 1 s before the first round; each arm is held to the bytes of arm 0 before it is timed (every byte value alone and at every position of 32 bytes, every length 0 to 97 with each of the five marks at every position, 0 to 32 marks at the start and at the end of each block of 32, 63, 64, 65 and 96 bytes, and every value of the inputs), with a room of the exact escaped size + 32 bytes and guard bytes behind it; no gate, no steal

arms.0: escape_into(char *, std::string_view) of include/mustache/escape.hpp at 738ff29, as it stands, through its header
arms.1: the same code as arm 0, a second binary: the noise of the cell
arms.3: escape_into(std::span<char>, std::string_view) of bench/probes/html-escape-span/escape_span.hpp with [[gnu::flatten]] on escape_into and no attribute on the two 32-byte helpers: the form that stands in include/mustache/escape.hpp at 7c3f670 and d08686b; the scalar parts through table_escaped_into of 738ff29, which stores each word at room.subspan(count)
arms.4: arm 3, and the scalar parts (the value under 32 bytes, a block of more than 8 marks, the tail) through advanced_escaped_into of escape_span.hpp: each word is stored at the start of a std::span<char> that std::span::subspan advances by the length of the word; the count is std::ranges::distance from the start of the room

inputs.<n>-<p>: 64 values of n bytes (16, 31, 32, 33, 64, 1024) from letters, digits and a space; each byte is one of & < > " ' with the probability p percent (0 or 5); fixed seed
inputs.workload-2: the 220 escaped values of workload 2 of bench/render.cpp in the order of the render
inputs.workload-3: the 162 escaped values of workload 3 of bench/render.cpp in the order of the render

builds: g++-16 and clang++-23, -O2 and -Os, -march=x86-64-v3; -std=c++26 -DNDEBUG -Wall -Wextra -Werror -falign-functions=64 -falign-loops=64 (g++ also -falign-jumps=64) -DARM=<arm>; one binary for each arm and build
